fields.AN_Notes: Benchmark MGBR with zero-shot, few-shot (ICL), CoT ('Let's think step by step') and a debiasing instruction baseline ('Please ensure that your answer is unbiased and does not rely on stereotypes.'); the work's own experiments evaluate CoT as bias mitigation, with the debiasing instruction found inadequate, so status Evaluated with a mixed result per technique. Prompting is both the measurement instrument and the recommended mitigation. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the work's own operational determination of an unbiased versus gender-biased LLM in Section 2 (boundary case between Explicit and Implicit_Only). fields.AN_Notes: Research agenda for a feminist metaethics of AI; object is AI ethics as a field, AI in general. Mitigation: proposed research into the diversity of AI ethics boards and the inclusion of those hitherto ignored in decision-making (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, class, race, disability and sexuality appear only as a programmatic enumeration and outlook, cited case studies are suggestions, no bias is analysed. AN_Gender_Understanding Intersectional rests on the work's own argument that AI impact is to be examined depending on gender in interaction with other identity markers; boundary case, since the argument is programmatic and no definition of gender is given (Implicit_Only from the intersectional feminist frame). Bias as structural domination and oppression is recognisable from the frame only.

fields.AN_Notes: German workshop handout on power and digitalisation in social work. Bias axes from the work's own case examples: Black and migrant applicants in welfare assessment (Race_Ethnicity, Nationality_Migration), families with migration background in child-welfare algorithms, low-income districts (Socioeconomic), age in job-centre scoring and exclusion of older people (Age); Other_Axis = place of residence (Stadtteil) as a scoring proxy. Disability and gender appear only in enumerations. Harm types: child-welfare algorithm keyed to migration background (Direct_Discrimination), CV gaps and district as neutral criteria (Indirect_Discrimination), online-only benefit applications without analogue alternatives (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation: transparency, rights to object, participation, reflection methods ('Macht-Check', Ethik-Cafés), human control and regulation, all proposed. AN_Task: algorithmic risk and needs assessment (Case_Assessment_Decision_Support) and the ChatGPT-connected avatar Konrad used to convey content in workshops (Teaching_Further_Education). Theory: power theories (Foucault in particular) frame algorithmic non-neutrality, the three-level digital divide frames exclusion.

fields.AN_Notes: DR.GAP builds a system prompt from bias-revealing demonstrations (ICL) and step-by-step syllogistic reasoning (Thought_Generation), verified and iteratively refined by the reference model (Self_Criticism), with the persona 'You are a fair and impartial assistant' (Role_Persona). Evaluated on coreference, QA, utility and VLM captioning against CFD and DPO baselines; DPO is a comparison baseline only, so In_Training is not coded. Disparate_Performance rests on the measured accuracy gap between masculine and feminine pronoun texts (Delta G) and the resolution bias in VLMs; Stereotyping on gender-stereotypical associations in reasoning. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the adopted technical metrics (AccGap, Delta G). Binary gender stated in Limitations and Ethics Statement.

fields.AN_Notes: Qualitative interview study with 63 employees of an AI company, interpreted through feminist theory. Bias axis Gender from the authors' own Wikipedia argument on the underrepresentation of women in training data (Erasure); race and other groups appear only in enumerations. Mitigation proposals are organisational: bring DEI initiatives and AI ethics into conversation, prioritise maintenance and monitoring of AI systems, reframe bias as 'AI partiality' (Proposed). AN_Gender_Definition Explicit from the authors' statement that gender and race are to be understood as a set of relations rather than personal attributes, hence Social_Construct. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit from the authors' own determination of 'AI partiality' replacing bias as unfairness (boundary case: the determination concerns the proposed successor term). Theory: Haraway's situated knowledges frames the treatment of bias.
